name: Cedar County, IA
findings: Cedar County has 88 nonprofit organizations. 24 of them (27%) list at least one way to get involved in their tax returns or on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is membership, listed by 19 organizations.
Social and fraternal organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (59% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Cedar County has about as many organizations offering opportunities per resident.
29% of the organizations offering opportunities have no identified type, so the breakdown by type is partial.

observations.title: Fewer organizations list volunteering
observations.text: Per resident, fewer organizations in Cedar County list volunteering in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 70% of the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 14 organizations here; 47% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Does that match what people here experience? Where do people find ways to volunteer now, including outside formal organizations?

observations.title: Social and fraternal organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 9 social and fraternal organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity in their tax returns or on their websites. Many may still offer them without describing them there.

observations.title: Social and fraternal organizations stand out for volunteering
